title: Head of Credit & Fraud
description: ABOUT HAPPY MONEY Happy Money is a consumer finance company that empowers people to achieve their goals through simple, transparent loans funded by trusted financial institutions. Through its proprietary lending platform, Hive, Happy Money delivers a fully digital experience that simplifies borrowing for consumers and helps credit unions, banks and asset managers diversify balance sheets and scale with confidence. Happy Money’s end-to-end loan origination and participation programs provide partners with turnkey access to high-performing assets, underpinned by disciplined credit expertise and robust risk management. Together with its lending partners, Happy Money has originated more than $7 billion in loans to help nearly 350,000 people take greater control of their financial futures. Learn more at happymoney.com. View our Employee Privacy Policy here. Happy Money is a 100% fully distributed company. Remote work doesn’t mean less work, we work full-time jobs and show up to them fully every day. To learn more about our values and the way we work, review our Happy Money Way Overview! ABOUT THE ROLE Happy Money is looking for a Head of Credit & Fraud to own credit and fraud risk strategy for our lending business. Reporting to the Chief Risk & Analytics Officer, you will set credit and fraud policy, lead the team and be the senior credit voice with our Executive Leadership Team and capital partners. You will balance growth and losses to maximize risk-adjusted returns through the credit cycle and build business cases that show a clear, achievable path to profitable implementation. You are highly data driven and committed to testing and learning. You bring the executive presence to explain credit decisions clearly to leaders, partners and investors, and you are happy to dig into the data yourself when the work calls for it. RESPONSIBILITIES Credit & Fraud Strategy Own credit and fraud strategy and policy across the customer lifecycle, from acquisition and underwriting through account management, to maximize risk-adjusted returns and manage losses through the credit cycle Set credit risk appetite with the Chief Risk Officer and translate it into clear credit policy, approval criteria and loss targets Balance loss rates, approval rates and conversion to grow profitably, and lead the rollout of growth initiatives, measured against credit and profitability targets Run a disciplined test-and-learn agenda across credit and fraud strategies, with clear success metrics and regular readouts Own credit performance monitoring, vintage analysis and early-warning indicators, and partner with Data Science and Finance on loss forecasting and model governance Spot credit and fraud risks early, including shifts in consumer credit health and new fraud patterns, and respond with timely policy and control changes With Legal & Compliance, make sure credit and fraud policies meet regulatory, fair lending and partner requirements Leadership Recruit, develop and lead a high-performing team of credit, fraud and strategy professionals; set clear goals, coach for growth and hold the team to a high standard Build the right mix of in-house talent, third-party partners and automation tools (including AI), and know when to use each Set the operating rhythm for the function, including credit committee materials, portfolio performance reviews, a central knowledge base and regular leadership updates Build a culture of accountability, curiosity and sound judgment, and grow future leaders on the team Executive & Cross-Functional Partnership Partner with the Executive Leadership Team on company strategy, annual planning, growth targets and risk appetite, and bring a clear credit point of view to growth and investment decisions Present credit and fraud performance, forecasts, risks and recommendations to the Executive Leadership Team, and support reporting to the Board of Directors Work across the organization with Pricing, Data Science, Data Strategy, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, Capital Markets, Finance and Legal & Compliance to design, launch and scale credit and fraud strategies Partner with Product and Engineering on the decisioning, data and tooling roadmap that credit and fraud strategies depend on Own the end-to-end analytics workflow for the function, including defining success and performance metrics, sharing them company-wide and building actionable dashboards and reports Capital Partners Be the senior credit contact for Happy Money's capital partners, including credit unions, banks and institutional investors Present portfolio performance, credit policy changes and loss expectations to capital partners, and answer their credit questions plainly and with data Work with Capital Markets on partner credit criteria, new partner onboarding and credit programs that support funding capacity Lead the credit portion of partner and investor due diligence, audits and reviews, including forward flow, loan sale and financing discussions ABOUT YOU Core Qualifications College degree in a quantitative discipline such as Economics, Finance, Engineering, Math, Statistics, Business, Science or Computer Science (or equivalent experience) 12+ years of experience in financial services 8+ years of credit risk experience, including direct ownership of credit strategy or credit policy decisions for a consumer lending portfolio Experience owning or partnering closely on fraud risk strategy and controls Proven track record of building, leading and developing high-performing teams, including remote, multidisciplinary teams Demonstrated experience building trust across cross-functional teams, cultivating an environment of productive friction where feedback is given freely and effectively Experience presenting substantiating data-driven strategic decisions to C-suite executives, boards and external partners or investors with a high degree of influence Direct experience working with capital partners, bank partners, lenders or investors on credit performance, due diligence or credit program design Track record of working across Product, Engineering, Data Science and Operations to build and scale credit and fraud decisioning processes and systems Working knowledge of consumer lending regulation, including fair lending (ECOA / Regulation B), FCRA and model risk management Highly data driven, with the technical fluency to challenge models, analyses and dashboards directly Experience balancing individual contributions with people-management needs across an organization and knows when to transition from strategy to execution (and vice-versa) Preferred Qualifications Experience at a fintech or smaller financial services company, where leaders combine strategy with hands-on execution Experience in unsecured consumer lending, such as personal loans or credit cards Experience with bank or credit union partnership models, forward flow or loan sale programs Experience writing a credit policy as part of a new product launch Experience managing a consumer lending portfolio through a credit downturn Advanced degree (MBA, or MS / PhD in a quantitative field) BENEFITS & PERKS Generous medical, dental, and vision insurance options Eligible for Annual Bonus Eligible for Long-term Incentive Program 401k Plan with a matching contribution Generous PTO including sick leave, vacation, volunteer, and more 12 Weeks Paid Parental Leave Company-paid short & long term disability and life insurance Monthly tech stipend to help cover expenses for remote work Happy Money is a 100% fully distributed workforce Base Salary Range $220,000—$260,000 USD

title: Senior Audit Manager-Investments
description: About AIG American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Founded in 1919, today AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement products, and other financial services to customers in more than 80 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risks and provide for retirement security. AIG common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Internal Audit Group AIG’s Internal Audit Group (IAG) provides independent and objective assurance, advice, and insight guided by a philosophy of adding value to improve the operations of AIG. IAG assists AIG in accomplishing its objectives by bringing a systematic and disciplined approach to evaluate and improve the effectiveness of AIG’s control environment including risk management, operational, financial, internal control, and governance processes. As a Senior Manager, you will be part of IAG’s Finance Audit Team in the New York, NY office. You will collaborate with Investment stakeholders, IAG and other assurance teams to: Partner with the business to identify and analyze the inherent risks in Investments and the controls that management has implemented to mitigate their risks. Lead Investment audits including SOX testing coverage to ensure that audit projects and stakeholders focus on key risks and controls. Present audit findings, risk insights, and recommendations to senior management. Educate stakeholders on the IAG process and work to improve the overall audit experience. Contribute to the overall effectiveness and value of IAG by recommending and developing innovative approaches and solutions (e.g. the use of data analytics, automation, and Agile audit methodology) Proactively identify and propose efficiencies and rationalization opportunities to stakeholders. Contribute to the overall effectiveness and value of IAG by recommending and developing innovative approaches and solutions (e.g. the use of data analytics and automation). IAG is seeking a highly engaged and experienced audit professional, or someone with equivalent industry experience, with strong technical and interpersonal competencies and people management skills to contribute to IAG’s mission of being an industry leading internal audit team and key contributor to the achievement of the firm’s strategic goals. We are looking for candidates that are proactive, continuously learn and introduce improved ways of doing things, both to business stakeholders in development of solutions to problems, IAG processes, including the use of data analytics. The ideal candidates will be bold thinkers with an entrepreneurial bent and will possess a powerful blend of IQ (technical skills, consistent learning, statistical & financial acumen), and emotional intelligence [EQ] (adaptive communication, empathy, listening skills, challenging with humility). IAG also looks for diverse backgrounds of experience, culture and thought. Successful candidates typically have a global perspective and a record of successful teamwork. You will be part of a large and diverse firm working within a team-oriented environment. You will gain a unique view of AIG, as part of planning and executing on all aspects of the audit process and risk assessment activities and will build close working relationships with business and functional leaders, colleagues across other assurance functions, and fellow team members. Specific Responsibilities Lead risk-based internal audits across investment activities and related financial processes. Oversee SOX 404 compliance efforts, including control design evaluation, testing, deficiency assessment, and remediation tracking. Assess controls over investment valuation, financial reporting, portfolio accounting, treasury activities, and capital management. Partner with Finance leadership to identify control gaps, operational inefficiencies, and emerging risks. Review complex financial transactions, accounting estimates, and judgments for accuracy and compliance with policies and standards. Drive continuous improvement initiatives by recommending enhancements to controls, processes, and governance frameworks. Supervise and mentor audit staff, providing technical guidance, coaching, and performance feedback. Coordinate with external auditors on SOX reliance, testing strategies, and issue resolution. Utilize data analytics and technology-enabled audit techniques to enhance audit effectiveness and efficiency. Support enterprise risk assessment activities and contribute to annual audit planning. Clearly and concisely communicate audit results or other key messages to a variety of constituents, including senior business and audit management, and regulators, and advise on emerging industry or regulatory topics/issues that may impact audit coverage. When you join our team, you’ll unlock a motivating and impactful career—growing your skills and advancing your profession within one of the world’s leading financial services institutions. We are seeking a strategic, collaborative, and forward-thinking leader for this critical manager role in the FRC team. This position provides support for the oversight of SOX and MAR controls inclusive of those that span across Prudential Global Investment Management (PGIM). You will also provide support for ongoing transformations, change leadership, and continuous improvement in Prudential’s evolving risk and control landscape with respect to internal controls over financial reporting. Additionally, you will also help foster a culture of trust, inclusion, and continuous improvement, aligned with Prudential’s core values. The current EWA for this position is Hybrid and requires your on-site presence 3 days per week. Your manager will provide additional details relative to days you are expected to be on-site. What you'll do: Main contact to provide support for PGIM’s extensive number of SOX and MAR controls. Support financial reporting control efforts by assisting in the identification, design and testing of key controls for new and evolving strategic initiatives, ensuring robust risk management and regulatory compliance throughout transformation. Assist in identifying and developing control issues as they arise, analyzing root causes, and partnering with management to design and implement meaningful actions that address underlying problems, ensuring control design is adequate and enhanced controls are operating effectively. Coordinate extensively with Prudential’s control partners, including Internal Audit, PGIM’s Operational Risk and Compliance teams, and the Company’s external auditor, PwC, to ensure alignment, transparency, and effective execution of risk and control initiatives. Serve as a trusted advisor and partner across the enterprise, fostering stakeholder relationships and upholding Prudential’s standards of integrity. The successful candidate will drive the integration of risk and control considerations into transformation design, promote the adoption of automated and preventive controls, and ensure that Finance remains aligned with enterprise policies, governance standards, and regulatory expectations throughout periods of change. title: SAP Technical Lead
description: GAQ126R43 About Databricks At Databricks, our mission is to help data teams solve the world's toughest problems—and that begins with empowering our own employees with exceptional internal products. The Databricks IT organization is a product-led engineering team building intelligent, AI-powered platforms that simplify how work gets done across the company. For Finance, our vision is to eliminate manual, repetitive work by automating complex business processes, surfacing actionable insights, and orchestrating end-to-end workflows. We are reimagining finance operations so teams spend less time processing transactions, chasing approvals, and resolving exceptions, and more time delivering strategic insights that accelerate the business. We're looking for an SAP Technical Lead to own the technical architecture and delivery of our SAP platform. In this role, you'll define the technical vision for a clean-core S/4HANA landscape, lead the engineers who build on it, and architect the intelligent, agentic AI layer that sits between SAP and the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You'll set the standards, make the hard build-versus-adopt calls, and ensure everything we ship is secure, performant, and built to scale. The Opportunity SAP will serve as the foundation for Databricks' core finance processes, including Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, and Order-to-Cash. As the SAP Technical Lead, you will own how those processes are engineered—from the clean-core S/4HANA core and its extensions, to the integration fabric that connects SAP to the rest of the enterprise, to the AI and agentic services that make the experience intelligent. Rather than accumulating custom code inside the digital core, you'll champion a modern extensibility model on SAP BTP and the Databricks Lakehouse, so Finance teams get automated, AI-driven workflows on top of a core that stays clean, upgradable, and fast. Your mission is to combine the strength of SAP with the power of Databricks AI to build a technical foundation that lets the business scale. What You'll Do Own the Technical Architecture: Define and own the end-to-end technical architecture for the S/4HANA landscape (greenfield, brownfield, or selective data transition), aligned to clean-core principles, with clear guardrails that keep the digital core standard and upgrade-ready. Lead the Extensibility Strategy: Define and own the extensibility strategy for SAP, using Databricks-native applications to address business requirements beyond core SAP capabilities. Establish clear architecture and governance standards to ensure extensions are scalable, secure, and aligned with the broader Finance technology strategy. Drive Enterprise AI Integration: Drive a strong integration with ongoing Enterprise AI transformation within Databricks by bringing AI fluency and hands on AI experience. Design the Integration Fabric: Architect secure, resilient integration across SAP and non-SAP systems using SAP Integration Suite, event-driven patterns, APIs, OData v4, and change-data feeds into the Lakehouse, with clear contracts, error handling, and observability. Unify SAP Data in the Lakehouse: Partner with data engineering on the technical patterns for landing SAP data in Databricks—ingestion, CDC, semantic and master-data modeling, lineage, and governance. Set Engineering Standards: Establish CI/CD, automated testing, and transport/deployment pipelines for BTP artifacts; own code and design reviews; and define the technical standards, security patterns, and best practices the team builds against. Lead the Team: Mentor developers and architects, lead technical steering, and act as the connective tissue across the SAP ecosystem (BTP, Integration Suite) and the systems around it, partnering closely with functional, product, and partner engineering teams. Be Accountable for Non-Functionals: Own performance, scalability, security, resilience, and cost across the landscape; report technical status, risks, and roadmaps to stakeholders. What You Bring 10+ years in SAP technical roles , with 3+ years as a technical lead or architect, and a proven track record delivering at least one full S/4HANA program (greenfield or conversion) plus BTP-based extension delivery. Clean-Core Architecture: Deep, hands-on command of clean-core principles—custom-code assessment and remediation, in-app vs. side-by-side extensibility, released APIs and extension points, and the governance that keeps the core clean over time. SAP BTP & Modern Development: Advanced experience across SAP BTP, ABAP Cloud and the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP), CDS, and CAP, with Fiori/SAPUI5 on the front end. AI & Agentic Systems: Hands-on experience or strong technical command of agentic automation, LLM orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation—plus clear judgment about where AI belongs in a controlled, auditable ERP process and where it does not. Integration & APIs: Advanced experience with SAP Integrat
